disclaimer: UAE tax rules changed materially through 2025/2026. From 1 January 2026 the VAT Law amendments (FDL 16/2025), the Tax Procedures Law amendments (FDL 17/2025), and the sweetened drinks tiered excise all apply, and a new AML law (FDL 10/2025) has been in force since 14 October 2025. Small Business Relief now covers eligible tax periods ending through 31 December 2029 under Ministerial Decision 131 of 2026. The e-invoicing pilot went live on 1 July 2026; businesses with revenue at or above AED 50M must appoint an Accredited Service Provider by 30 October 2026 (Ministerial Resolution 66 of 2026). Minimum excise prices for specified tobacco and vaping products apply from 1 September 2026 under Cabinet Decision 137 of 2026. The unified late-payment penalty (Cabinet Decision 129 of 2025) took effect 14 April 2026. Always verify against the FTA and MoF portals before quoting figures. From 1 October 2026 the amended VAT Executive Regulation (Cabinet Decision 149 of 2026), FTA Decision 13 of 2026 on supplier and supply verification before input tax deduction, and FTA Decision 17 of 2026 on input tax for employee expenses all apply. FTA Decision 12 of 2026 sets Pillar Two (DMTT) registration timelines, with a 30 November 2026 deadline for fiscal years ending before 30 April 2026. Corporate Tax returns for calendar-year 2025 periods are due by 30 September 2026.

qfzp.name: Qualifying Free Zone Person
qfzp.summary: Eligible free zone persons get 0% on Qualifying Income and 9% on the rest. The ordinary AED 375,000 0% band and Small Business Relief do not apply to a QFZP.
qfzp.saas_note: SaaS is not itself a named Qualifying Activity. Qualification depends on the counterparty, excluded activities and any qualifying intellectual-property income; do not assume all SaaS revenue is non-qualifying. QFZPs do not receive the ordinary AED 375,000 band on non-qualifying taxable income.
qfzp.de_minimis: Lower of 5% of revenue or AED 5,000,000

small_business_relief.name: Small Business Relief
small_business_relief.law: Ministerial Decision 73 of 2023, as amended by Ministerial Decision 131 of 2026
small_business_relief.summary: Eligible resident persons with revenue at or below AED 3M may elect Small Business Relief for tax periods beginning on or after 1 June 2023 and ending on or before 31 December 2029.

registration.waiver_announcement: April 2025: penalty waived if first return is filed within 7 months of the end of the tax period.

current_cycle.note: The FTA confirmed that all Taxable Persons with a financial year ended 31 December 2025, including Small Business Relief electors, must file and pay by 30 September 2026. Other year ends follow the 9-month rule.

pillar_two_dmtt.name: Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax
pillar_two_dmtt.applies_to: MNE groups with consolidated revenue at or above EUR 750 million

registration_status.status: FTA Decision 12 of 2026 (issued 16 July 2026, published 4 August 2026) sets DMTT registration timelines: register within 7 months of the end of the first in-scope fiscal year, but an entity with a fiscal year ending before 30 April 2026 must register on or before 30 November 2026. A Domestic Designated Filing Entity registers on behalf of the domestic group. Ministerial Decision 133 of 2026 separately identifies Pillar Two Information Return filers. Confirm operational filing requirements with the FTA.
registration_status.first_return_note: First top-up tax return (for FY ending 31 December 2025) is expected due 30 June 2027 under an 18-month transitional window. Verify with the FTA.
registration_status.registration_deadline_general: Within 7 months from the end of the first fiscal year in which the entity is in scope
registration_status.registration_deadline_transitional_appli: Entities with a fiscal year ending before 2026-04-30 (for example, calendar-year 2025)
registration_status.deregistration: Apply within 6 months of ceasing to exist or of the end of the fiscal year in which the entity leaves the MNE group; entities ceasing before 30 June 2026 must apply by 31 December 2026. Out-of-scope notifications are due within 6 months of the tested fiscal year end.

information_return.summary: Requires Pillar Two Information Returns for in-scope UAE constituent entities (excluding investment entities), UAE joint ventures and JV subsidiaries, and UAE-created stateless reverse hybrids. A designated local entity may file on behalf of covered entities.
information_return.foreign_filing_relief: Local filing is relieved where a qualifying return is filed by an ultimate parent or designated filing entity in a jurisdiction with a qualifying competent authority agreement effective for the reporting year; the FTA must still be notified of the filing entity identity and location.

sports_entities_exemption.summary: Qualifying non-commercial sports entities (international sports entities, sports entities, and supporting ancillary entities) are exempt from corporate tax retroactively from 1 June 2023. Conditions include recognition by the Ministry of Sports or competent authority and exclusive use of income and assets for the entity's objectives; entities must register and apply for the exemption with the FTA and file an annual declaration.

exemption_applications.summary: Exempt-category persons under Article 4(1)(f) to (i) of the Corporate Tax Law (qualifying public benefit entities, qualifying investment funds, pension and social security funds, qualifying wholly owned subsidiaries and Cabinet-designated persons) must register under the FTA Decision 3 of 2024 timelines and then apply for exemption no later than 90 business days after the end of the tax period in which they met the conditions.
special_deadlines: Persons covered by Cabinet Decision 55 of 2025 applying retrospectively: by 2026-12-31.

Persons covered by a Cabinet decision issued on or after 2026-01-01 (for example Cabinet Decision 1 of 2026 on sports entities) applying retrospectively: within 90 business days from the end of the tax period in which the decision was issued.
Qualifying limited partnership juridical persons under Article 5 of Cabinet Decision 34 of 2025, for 2025 tax periods ending on or before 2026-08-31: by 2026-12-31.
Wholly owned subsidiaries of government or government-controlled entities for tax periods ending before 2026-01-01: by 2026-10-31.

fta_service_fees.note: Cabinet Decision 174 of 2025 revised FTA service fees from 1 January 2026: new fees for Unilateral Advance Pricing Agreement applications, and the paid paper Tax Registration Certificate and Warehouse Keeper Registration Certificate replaced by free electronic certificates with QR-code verification.

guides_2026.note: June 2026 FTA publications: updated Corporate Tax Guide on Taxation of Family Foundations (CTGFF1, 10 June 2026), Education Sector VAT Guide (29 June 2026), and a Basic Tax Information Bulletin on Corporate Tax Losses (25 June 2026). Per secondary legal reporting; verify titles and dates on the FTA guides page.

changes: Reverse-charge imports no longer require self-issued tax invoices.
Carry-forward of excess recoverable VAT is capped at 5 years from the end of the tax period in which it arose; 2021 credits start expiring during 2026.
The FTA may deny input VAT recovery on supply chains connected to tax evasion where the recipient knew.
The VAT Law statute-of-limitations article moved into the Tax Procedures Law.

directives_2026.binding_basis: Article 54 bis of the Tax Procedures Law provides for directives binding on the FTA and taxpayers within scope.

directives.topic: VAT adjustments after a registrant exits a tax group
Conversion of digital currency values into AED
Fees and charges in life insurance and life reinsurance contracts
Valuation of deemed supplies of services

directives_2026.note: The FTA VAT legislation register lists these five directives published in July 2026. Apply each directive using its original text; this inventory does not reproduce detailed transaction treatments.

supply_verification_2026.subject: Measures, procedures and conditions required by taxable persons to verify the validity and integrity of supplies before deducting input tax (Article 54 bis of the VAT Law).
key_requirements: Verify supplier identity: ID and a meeting for natural persons; incorporation records and the authorised representative's ID for legal persons.
Verify the supplier's actual place of business and its fit with the supplier's activities.
Check risk indicators (more than two address or key-staff changes in 12 months, disproportionate transactions) and keep a justified explanation if any apply.
Where supplies from the supplier exceed or are expected to exceed AED 375,000 over 12 months, obtain a UAE bank confirmation of the supplier's account and review public reviews and media.
Assess commercial rationale, payment method (electronic by default; cash only with a documented reason and within legal thresholds), pricing and the supplier's licensed activity.

executive_regulation_amendments_2026.deferred_provisions: The revised input tax apportionment rules apply from the first tax year commencing after 1 October 2027.
changes: Updated supply and import rules for medical products to match the current healthcare legislative framework.
Clarified input tax recovery on employee accommodation.
Aligned the Capital Assets Scheme scope with the VAT Law.
Refined the input tax apportionment method (existing rules retained for government entities and charities).
New provisions on single composite supplies based on economic substance.
Input tax is not recoverable where consideration above a threshold set by a Minister of Finance decision is paid in cash.
executive_regulation_amendments_2026.cash_threshold_note: The cash-payment threshold is to be prescribed by a separate Ministerial decision; it is not asserted here.

employee_expenses_input_tax_2026.summary: Sets the cases and conditions for recovering input tax on goods or services provided free to employees under a contractual obligation or documented policy: transport between home and work or for job duties, food in remote locations without facilities, work-required accommodation, temporary accommodation of up to 30 days for new employees, work phones and data under a documented and monitored policy, and business parking fees. In each case the employee must not be able to take a cash alternative where the decision so requires.

tax_procedures.name: Tax Procedures Law amendments
tax_procedures.law: Federal Decree-Law 17 of 2025 (amending Federal Decree-Law 28 of 2022)

audit_window.summary: The standard 5-year audit and assessment window is extendable up to 15 years for tax evasion or failure to register, and the FTA gets 4 extra years to complete an audit notified before the window expires.

refunds_and_credit_balances.basis: Refunds and credit balances are claimable for a maximum of 5 years from the end of the relevant tax period.
refunds_and_credit_balances.transition: Balances older than 5 years are claimable only until 31 December 2026 under a 1-year transition.

tax_procedures.excise_statute_of_limitations: Consolidated into the Tax Procedures Law; the Excise Tax Law's standalone limitation article was repealed by FDL 17/2025.

esr.name: Economic Substance Regulations
esr.status: DEAD for financial years ending after 2022-12-31
esr.applies_to_periods: Financial years commencing on or after 2019-01-01 and ENDING on or before 2022-12-31. Scope is set by the financial year END date, so a year running into 2023 is already out of scope.
esr.historical_obligations: NOT waived. Cabinet Decision 98 of 2024 cancelled only the requirement to file notifications and reports for financial years ending after 2022-12-31. For in-scope years (2019 to 2022) companies remain liable to file, to answer information and amendment requests from the FTA or the regulatory authority, and to pay any penalties already imposed. Penalties for in-scope years are not refundable.
esr.warning: Do NOT promise ESR filing tools for current periods. The 9 Relevant Activities only matter for historical filings. Do not tell a user that historical ESR penalties are refundable, because they are not.

key_changes: Fines for legal persons raised to AED 5,000,000 to AED 100,000,000.
Tax evasion added as a predicate offence.
aml_cft.historical_note: FDL 10/2025 replaces the Federal Decree-Law 20 of 2018 regime; FDL 20/2018 remains relevant only as a historical reference for pre-October-2025 matters.
aml_cft.regulator: Activity-specific supervisory authority; MOET supervises the listed DNFBP sectors in mainland UAE and commercial free zones.
dnfbp_categories: Dealers in precious metals and stones

vara.name: Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority of Dubai
vara.applies_to: Virtual asset service providers operating in Dubai (excluding DIFC)

issuance_rulebook_2026.note: April 2026: VARA published its first dedicated Virtual Asset Issuance Rulebook guidance, covering fiat-referenced and asset-referenced tokens and banning anonymity-enhanced cryptocurrencies (AECs), alongside a formal virtual asset derivatives regime.

aml_cft.reporting_authority: UAE Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), through goAML

ubo.name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner
ubo.law: Cabinet Decision 109 of 2023 (Regulation of the Real Beneficiary Procedures)
ubo.previous_law: Cabinet Decision 58 of 2020, superseded with effect from 2023-11-16. Cite it only for conduct predating that date.

penalties.instrument: Cabinet Decision 132 of 2023 (issued 2023-12-15, superseded Cabinet Decision 53 of 2021)
penalties.structure: Graduated per violation: written warning for a first breach, up to AED 50,000 for a second, up to AED 100,000 for a third, plus possible licence suspension.

ubo.summary: In-scope UAE legal persons must maintain and file beneficial-owner information with their registrar. The 25% ownership/voting test is supplemented by control tests; government-owned and financial-free-zone exceptions require separate treatment.

excise.law: Federal Decree-Law 7 of 2017 (as amended by Federal Decree-Law 17 of 2025)

sweetened_drinks_volumetric.model: Tiered volumetric excise by sugar content, replacing the flat 50% ad valorem rate on sweetened beverages.
sweetened_drinks_volumetric.exempt: Drinks under 5g sugar per 100ml, or sweetened only with artificial sweeteners.
sweetened_drinks_volumetric.certification: A MoIAT Emirates Conformity Certificate is required to evidence sugar content; uncertified drinks default to the high-sugar band (AED 1.09 per litre).

minimum_excise_prices.products: Cigarettes, including conventional and heated cigarettes
Water-pipe tobacco, ready-to-use tobacco, and similar products
Liquids used in electronic smoking devices and tools, whether or not containing nicotine

e_invoicing.name: UAE E-Invoicing
e_invoicing.model: PINT AE on a Decentralized Continuous Transaction Control and Exchange (DCTCE) 5-corner model; e-invoices exchanged via accredited service providers (ASPs) and reported to the FTA through EmaraTax
e_invoicing.status: pilot phase live: the 5-corner model has been operational since July 2026 (pilot launched 2026-07-01 with a selected Taxpayer Working Group; voluntary adoption open to any business). At its 27 September 2026 Ras Al Khaimah awareness event the MoF reconfirmed the 30 October 2026 ASP appointment deadline and 1 January 2027 go-live for businesses with revenue at or above AED 50M.

revenue_at_or_above_aed_50m.note: The go-live date is unchanged despite the appointment extension.

asp_register.status: The official MoF page (last updated 28 September 2026) lists 60 accredited providers and 3 pre-approved providers under final accreditation assessment (up from 50 and 7 on 5 September 2026). It does not publish a separate overall pre-approved count; that count is unknown, not zero. Final assessment is not full accreditation.
asp_register.criteria_note: Accreditation criteria updated by Ministerial Resolution 56 of 2026: active Peppol-certified service providers that passed OpenPeppol conformance testing, with the PSP product operational for at least 2 years.

technical_docs.format: PINT AE XML (UBL-based) on the 5-corner DCTCE model

e_invoicing.scope_note: applies to B2B and B2G transactions; phased by revenue band

late_payment_penalty.name: Unified late-payment penalty
late_payment_penalty.basis: 14% per annum on unpaid tax, charged monthly at 14% divided by 12 for every month or part of a month, unifying the late-payment penalty across VAT, Excise and Corporate Tax (replacing the previous escalating monthly model)
late_payment_penalty.note: The calculator rounds any part month up to a whole charged month; confirm the exact calendar-month count with the FTA.

last_refresh_scope: Targeted refresh of 2026-09-28: refreshed the MoF ASP register to 60 accredited and 3 in final assessment and added the 27 September 2026 MoF reconfirmation of the e-invoicing deadlines; added Cabinet Decision 149 of 2026 amending the VAT Executive Regulation (effective 1 October 2026), FTA Decision 17 of 2026 on employee-expense input tax, the operative requirements and 1 October 2026 commencement of FTA Decision 13 of 2026, FTA Decision 12 of 2026 DMTT registration timelines (30 November 2026 transitional deadline), FTA Decision 15 of 2026 on exemption applications, and the 30 September 2026 Corporate Tax filing deadline for calendar-year 2025, all from MoF and FTA primary sources. Not re-verified: the expected 30 June 2027 first DMTT return date, transfer pricing thresholds, excise tiers and the AML, UBO and data-protection sections. Not a full re-verification of every field in this pack; full_review_date is preserved.
